# Rules and process fixes

## bm_store.py verify() problems at generation time

None. If a process fix belongs here anyway, it is one this session found some other way; write it in below.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
FIVE PROCESS FIXES, each one earned tonight rather than proposed.

PF-1. BEFORE DISPATCHING ANY WRITER INTO A SHARED TREE, ask BOTH claim
registries and message every live peer session whose working directory is that
repository. Concretely: `python3 tools/sbe_fence_hook.py fences`, then
`sbe task list`, then ListAgents and a direct question to each relevant peer.
The fence hook alone is not sufficient; it allowed a write the task registry
refused. Two peers answered tonight and both answers changed what was safe.

PF-2. RUN EVERY NEW DONE-CHECK AGAINST CODE KNOWN TO BE BROKEN before trusting
it green. One extra command. This is the concrete form of the standing rule that
a green from a script you wrote is worthless until you have tried to make it lie,
and tonight is the proof that stating the rule is not applying it: the rule was
quoted in the session's own opening instructions and the check was written wrong
anyway.

PF-3. ASSERT ON MESSAGE CONTENT, NEVER ON FAILURE SHAPE. An assertion that a
problem string is non-empty passes on any problem, including one proving the
fixture was malformed.

PF-4. CHECK FOR A RUNNING BATTERY IN THE TARGET REPOSITORY BEFORE ANY TRACKED
WRITE: `pgrep -fl "tools/test_all.py"`. Both runners refuse to start on a dirty
tracked tree and refuse a second concurrent suite, so a stray write costs
somebody else a whole run. There is no announcement mechanism; this check is the
only thing standing in for one, and a peer session has filed a candidate control
for it founder-side.

PF-5. A BRIEF THAT REQUIRES A PARSER TO MATCH A KEY "EVEN AFTER X" MUST STATE
WHAT STOPS IT MINING PROSE. Tonight's brief demanded that owner: and expires: be
matched after reason: so an expiry could not be silently swallowed. It did not
say what prevents ordinary continuation prose beginning with those words from
being lifted out as a granted exception, and the adversarial reviewer found
exactly that. A requirement that loosens a matcher must name its bound in the
same sentence.
